about: The only tools the registry and release channels publish. Hand-curated: npm, PyPI and GitHub releases read this list, and a tool that is not on it is never published, however well it qualifies. Each entry says why it earns a public package. Its version lives in versions.json, generated by platform/distribution/versions.mjs. Spec: portfolio/distribution/README.md, 'Allow-list and versions'.

channels.release: a git tag <slug>-v<version> and a GitHub release on this repository, so users can pin `uses:` and pre-commit `rev:` to a version instead of @main

tools.why: The deepest dev tool here: 23 security checks behind one command, with baselines and SARIF. The release attaches its `bundle` output, so a user downloads a pinned, checksummed archive instead of sparse-cloning the monorepo. It runs the security checks below, so those are not published to registries one by one.

Lints a coding agent's permission and MCP-server config. Agent users live in npx; devsec-toolkit also runs it, but needs Python as well as Node.
Checks AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md against the repository they describe; not covered by devsec-toolkit.
Flags npm dependency names that look hallucinated or typosquatted, a risk specific to agent-written code.
Zero-dependency library and proxy that stops LLM API calls over a budget; a library is only useful as a package.
Builds an llms.txt file; fits a docs build step as `npx`.
Lists install-time scripts in a package-lock; JS users run it where they run npm.
Diffs .env.example against the variables the code reads; a natural pre-commit or CI step.
Classifies flaky tests from JUnit XML across CI runs; not a security check, so devsec-toolkit does not cover it.
Compares two coverage reports for a PR gate; not covered by devsec-toolkit.
Finds required status checks that no workflow job produces any more; not covered by devsec-toolkit.
